{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001784","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: per the prs_model_evaluator trait-label guidance (trait_labels), phenotyping_reported is primary. All candidates have phenotyping_reported consistent with a direct AAA diagnosis (e.g., “Abdominal aortic aneurysm”; PGS000753 is “Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm”), so endpoint alignment does not separate them strongly.

Performance evidence and comparability: per prs_model_evaluator performance-metrics guidance (performance_metrics), PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only or covariates-regressed-out) are preferred over full-model AUROC/C-index that can be covariate-driven. PGS001784 uniquely provides a PRS-comparable metric: Nagelkerke R2 (covariates regressed out) = 0.014661, alongside a large EUR validation (n=350,767) and a modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS-auto; 911,440 variants). PGS002054 reports partial-r = 0.0144 but with much smaller validation (n=19,545). Other candidates mainly report full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS003973 C-index 0.882 with age/sex covariates; PGS003429 AUROC 0.708 with unknown covariates), which is less reliable for ranking standalone PRS quality.

Heritability sanity-check: local EUR h2 records returned by get_heritability_records for related ‘aortic aneurysm and dissection’ phenotypes show low observed-scale h2 but liability-scale h2 in the ~0.02–0.106 range, so a PRS-comparable R2 around ~0.015 is plausible and not obviously inconsistent with a heritability ceiling. 

Therefore, PGS001784 is the best-supported choice among the fixed candidates based on the cleanest PRS-specific performance evidence plus strong validation scale and contemporary genome-wide construction."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Skill evidence used (prs_model_evaluator):
- From trait_labels: phenotyping_reported is the primary endpoint-fidelity field; direct clinical disease endpoints are preferred over proxy/measurement traits.
- From performance_metrics: reported AUROC/C-index are typically full-model unless explicitly PGS-only; heavy clinical covariates can inflate full-model discrimination, so effect sizes (HR/OR per SD) and structural signals (method/variant coverage) matter when PGS-only metrics are absent.

Trait/endpoint alignment: PGS005252 is the cleanest direct match to the target trait aortic stenosis because it is labeled aortic stenosis (trait_reported/trait_efo) and its phenotyping_reported is a direct disease endpoint (“Incident aortic stenosis cases”). PGS005255/PGS005256 are more measurement-oriented (mean pressure gradient / peak aortic velocity) even though they mention aortic stenosis in trait_efo, so they are less endpoint-faithful per the trait_labels guidance. The hypertrophic cardiomyopathy scores are off-target.

Quality signals within the direct-match set: PGS005252 uses a modern genome-wide method (LDPred2) with very broad variant coverage (1,119,377 variants) and large European evaluation (n=446,895). Its reported C-index=0.87 is a full-model metric with multiple clinical covariates, so it is not treated as PRS-only performance; however, the HR=1.92 provides supportive evidence of meaningful stratification and is stronger than the HR reported for the other direct aortic stenosis score PGS005254 (HR=1.64; eval n=244,450; no AUC/C-index reported).

Heritability tool evidence (get_heritability_records): the lookup for “aortic stenosis” returned only unrelated “stenosis” traits (all match_score 0.0), so there is no reliable trait-specific h2 record available to contextualize PRS R²/AUC. This limits confidence but does not overturn the endpoint-fidelity and within-list evidence favoring PGS005252.

Conclusion: PGS005252 is the best available candidate for aortic stenosis in this fixed list, with direct endpoint alignment and the strongest overall evidence package despite the lack of PRS-only discrimination metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001344","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Grounded in prs_model_evaluator guidance (skill_overview + performance_metrics + publication_context) and asthma h2 lookup: For selecting among direct-match asthma PGS, prioritize endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out) over full-model AUROC, and discount framework-paper inflation/packaging. PGS001344 (Asthma diagnosed by doctor; snpnet; UKB) is the strongest candidate on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC (no covariates) 0.64568 and PGS-only R2 (no covariates) 0.05973, with only basic covariates in the full model (age, sex, array, PCs). Many alternatives either provide only full-model AUROC with heavier non-genetic predictors (e.g., PGS000799 includes familial/environmental/perinatal risk scores), only incremental R2 without PRS-only metrics (several portability/fine-mapping method comparisons), or come from broad framework contexts (e.g., the “across 813 traits in UK Biobank” family) where per-trait scores are not disease-optimized per publication_context guidance.\n\nHeritability sanity check (get_heritability_records, EUR asthma): local SNP-heritability estimates vary by definition/source, commonly ~0.05–0.19 (e.g., UKBB doctor-diagnosed asthma h2 around ~0.05; GWAS Atlas asthma up to ~0.19). PGS001344’s PGS-only R2 (~0.06) is plausible relative to these ceilings, supporting that its PRS-only performance is credible and not obviously a covariate-driven artifact. Therefore PGS001344 is the best-supported direct asthma PGS in this fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001340","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Grounded in prs_model_evaluator skill sections (skill_overview, trait_labels, performance_metrics) and the trait-specific h2 lookup:

- Endpoint fidelity (trait_labels): PGS001340 is a clean direct match for the target trait atrial fibrillation (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to AF). This is preferred over horizon-packaged endpoints (e.g., 5-year risk) or broader/combined endpoints unless those have clearly stronger comparable PRS-only evidence.

- Comparable PRS performance evidence (performance_metrics): PGS001340 reports explicit PRS-comparable metrics in Europeans (PGS AUROC no covariates ≈0.613; PGS R2 no covariates ≈0.023; incremental AUROC also reported). Per the skill, PRS-only metrics are the most reliable cross-model ranking axis; many other AF candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often with heavier clinical covariates such as CHARGE-AF) or only effect sizes, which are less directly comparable when PRS-only metrics exist.

- Heritability sanity check (get_heritability_records, EUR): local AF records show modest observed h2 (~0.02–0.03 in large GWAS-atlas/UKB-derived phenotypes; liability-scale varies by phenotype definition). PGS001340’s PRS-only R2 (~0.023) is plausible relative to these h2 values (not obviously exceeding a reasonable genetic-variance ceiling), supporting interpretability of the reported PRS-only metric.

Therefore, within this fixed candidate list, PGS001340 offers the best combination of direct AF endpoint alignment and clean, PRS-comparable performance reporting."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait/endpoint alignment (prs_model_evaluator trait_labels): the target is generic COPD. PGS001783 is a clean direct match across fields (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease”; trait_efo COPD). Several other candidates are related but less direct endpoints (emphysema; “chronic airway obstruction”; ICD10 J44; algorithmic-defined; time-to-event), which the trait_labels guidance treats as potentially acceptable but not inherently superior to a direct diagnosis endpoint.

Performance comparison (prs_model_evaluator performance_metrics): cross-model ranking should emphasize PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only or covariates-regressed-out) rather than full-model AUROC. PGS001783 reports a covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 = 0.0381, which is materially stronger PRS-specific evidence than the UKB snpnet COPD scores’ PGS-only R2 (~0.00235–0.00314) and more directly interpretable than partial correlation from the portability study.

Method/study context: PGS001783 uses PRS-CS-auto with very large variant coverage (~884k) and comes from a multi-biobank GWAS context, supporting robustness compared with sparse UKB-only snpnet models, especially given the stronger PRS-comparable R2.

Heritability sanity check (get_heritability_records for COPD): local EUR LDSC records for COPD-related endpoints (doctor-diagnosed COPD; ICD10 J44; self-reported COPD) show observed-scale h2 roughly in the ~0.003–0.025 range (liability-scale higher). The reported covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 of 0.038 is not obviously implausible given metric/scale differences and supports that PGS001783 captures meaningful genetic signal relative to the other candidates’ much smaller PRS-only R2."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000013","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS000013 is the strongest overall choice for the target trait coronary artery disease (CAD) among the provided candidates.

- Phenotype/endpoint fidelity: It is a direct CAD score (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Coronary artery disease”), matching the skill_overview emphasis on prioritizing endpoint alignment before comparing performance.
- Performance evidence quality: Per the performance_metrics guidance, PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only) are the most informative for cross-model ranking. PGS000013 reports a PRS-only/Nagelkerke R2=0.04 (and full-model AUROC=0.81 with basic covariates), whereas many alternatives report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often covariate-driven and not comparable across studies).
- Study/publication context: Its publication (“Genome-wide polygenic scores for common diseases identify individuals with risk equivalent to monogenic mutations.”, Nat Genet) is disease-endpoint-focused rather than a pan-trait portability framework signature (publication_context section), reducing concern that it is merely a high-throughput per-trait byproduct.
- Heritability sanity check: Local EUR heritability records for “coronary artery disease” show observed h2 roughly ~0.065–0.096 (with liability-scale values ~0.06–0.12 depending on record). A PRS-only R2 of 0.04 is plausible relative to this ceiling and not suggestive of scale mismatch or metric misuse.

Given these combined signals (direct endpoint + explicit PRS-only R2 + large European validation), PGS000013 is preferred over candidates with higher-looking full-model AUROC but no PRS-only metrics or with more packaging/covariate comparability uncertainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004254","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo: Crohn disease). Applying the PRS Model Evaluator procedure (read_skill_section: skill_overview) and performance interpretation guidance, the two snpnet models (PGS001330/PGS001331) come from a pan-phenome UK Biobank framework paper (“Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits in UK Biobank”), which the publication-context guidance flags as a common source of non-optimized per-disease scores (read_skill_section: publication_context). Their PRS-comparable metrics are modest (PGS-only AUROC ~0.576–0.579; PGS-only R² ~0.006–0.007). In contrast, PGS004254 is from a disease-relevant study context (immune-mediated colitis/Crohn-related application), uses a modern genome-wide method (LDpred2-auto) with far broader variant coverage (744,682 variants), and reports strong discriminative evidence via effect size (OR per SD 2.18, 95% CI 2.05–2.32) plus a high AUROC (0.72) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Heritability lookup for Crohn’s disease (get_heritability_records) shows substantial EUR SNP-heritability on the liability scale (~0.18–0.23 across multiple gwas_atlas records), supporting that meaningful genetic signal exists and making the very small PRS-only R² of the UKB framework scores less compelling as “best available” within this list. Confidence is moderate because PGS004254 lacks explicit PRS-only AUC/R², so its full-model AUROC cannot be treated as purely PRS-only; however, the strong OR and non-leaky covariate set provide the strongest available evidence of PRS discrimination among the candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004949","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: All candidates have trait_efo = dilated cardiomyopathy. Per trait-label guidance (read_skill_section: trait_labels), phenotyping_reported is the primary endpoint field and MTAG is not a mismatch; MTAG versions are mildly preferred within a study family when still targeting the same disease. PGS004949 is an MTAG-enhanced DCM score, though its phenotyping_reported is non-ischemic DCM (a narrower subtype than generic DCM), which is a mild endpoint-specificity trade-off.

Performance evidence: Per performance-metrics guidance (read_skill_section: performance_metrics), PRS-only metrics are the most comparable across candidates; full-model AUROC/R² can be covariate-driven and is weaker for cross-model ranking when PRS-only metrics are absent. PGS004949 reports explicit univariate (PRS-only) AUC = 0.68 (0.66–0.69) and strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.91), plus the largest PRS incremental contribution among the 2024-12-16 sibling set (liability-scale R² delta PRS/residual = 0.095). By contrast, PGS004861/PGS004862 report only full-model AUROC (~0.70–0.71) with basic covariates and no PRS-only AUC/R², making them less informative for standalone PRS quality.

Heritability sanity-check: get_heritability_records("dilated cardiomyopathy") returned EUR cardiomyopathy proxy records with low observed-scale h2 but moderate-to-high liability-scale h2 (e.g., h2_liability ~0.11–0.69). This supports that a meaningful genetic component is plausible for cardiomyopathy/DCM and does not obviously contradict the magnitude of PRS-only discrimination/effect size reported for PGS004949.

Why confidence is not High: PGS004949’s evaluation is in a MAE-labeled cohort (EVAL: MAE 100%), so transportability to other ancestries (and to broader all-cause DCM definitions) is not fully established from the provided metadata alone. Despite this, within the fixed candidate list it has the cleanest and strongest PRS-only evidence and is therefore the best overall choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001789","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct match and endpoint fidelity: PGS001789 targets gout directly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all gout), aligning with the evaluator’s recommendation to prioritize endpoint alignment before comparing metrics (read_skill_section: skill_overview). Performance evidence: it reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out; pgs_only_r2=0.031208) and has very large European validation (n=359,345). The evaluator notes PRS-only / covariates-regressed-out metrics are the most reliable cross-model signals, while full-model AUROC is often covariate-influenced and not directly comparable (read_skill_section: performance_metrics). Publication/study context: PGS001789 comes from a global biobank portability-focused paper (“Global Biobank analyses…”, Cell Genom), which the evaluator flags as a framework context that is useful but not automatically superior; however, in this candidate set it is still a direct gout endpoint with unusually strong validation scale and an explicit PRS-comparable metric, making it a robust choice versus candidates with only full-model AUROC or only effect sizes (read_skill_section: publication_context). Heritability sanity-check: local EUR LDSC records matching gout phenotypes show observed-scale h2 roughly 0.0006–0.048 and liability-scale h2 often ~0.05–0.36 depending on phenotype definition (get_heritability_records: gout). The reported PRS-comparable R2 (~0.031) is plausible relative to these ceilings and does not look implausibly inflated, supporting interpretability of the reported PRS contribution."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001320","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity (prs_model_evaluator skill_overview + trait_labels): PGS001320 is a direct match to the target trait hypertension across trait_reported/trait_efo and, critically, phenotyping_reported (primary endpoint-fidelity field). Competing candidates in the list are largely for type 2 diabetes or are hypertension variants with weaker evidence.

Performance evidence (prs_model_evaluator performance_metrics): PGS001320 reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.62908; PGS-only R2=0.06493) and incremental AUROC=0.04424, which is preferred for cross-model comparison over full-model AUROC alone. Its covariates are basic (age, sex, UKB array type, genotype PCs), reducing risk that performance is inflated by heavy clinical predictors.

Heritability sanity check (get_heritability_records, EUR): local LDSC records for hypertension include h2≈0.125–0.138 for “self-reported: hypertension” in UK Biobank; a PRS-only R2 of ~0.065 is plausible relative to this ceiling and not an obvious reporting artifact.

Within the direct hypertension set, PGS001320 also has stronger PRS-only AUROC/R2 than the closely related essential-hypertension snpnet scores (PGS000957/PGS000958), supporting it as the best overall candidate from this fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait/endpoint fidelity (prs_model_evaluator trait-label guidance): the target is “macular degeneration”. Candidates with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported explicitly matching age-related macular degeneration (AMD) are the most direct. PGS004606 has coherent alignment across fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all AMD), whereas PGS002269’s phenotyping_reported is retinal layer thickness (a biomarker/proxy endpoint) and PGS001013 is a broader UKB “Eye problems/disorders Macular degeneration” label.

Performance evidence (per performance-metrics guidance): PRS-only metrics are most comparable when present. PGS001013 reports PRS-only AUROC≈0.553 and PRS-only R2≈0.006 with very small incremental AUROC (~0.006), indicating weak standalone PRS signal despite a higher covariate-boosted full-model AUROC. Several other candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2; in that case, effect sizes can be supportive. PGS004606 reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.76) and full-model AUROC=0.71 with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) in a large European evaluation sample (n=163,011), making it the strongest overall evidence package among direct AMD endpoints. PGS004607 shows weaker AUROC (0.65) in the same evaluation ancestry, and PGS004952 has a very small validation sample (n=1,232) plus a suspiciously formatted AUROC value (84.2), reducing reliability.

Heritability sanity-check: local EUR h2 records for macular degeneration/AMD show non-trivial SNP heritability (e.g., Age-related Macular Degeneration h2≈0.067–0.190; UKB macular degeneration label h2≈0.010). This supports expecting modest-to-meaningful PRS discrimination; PGS004606’s strong OR and moderate AUROC are plausible within that context and more consistent with meaningful genetic signal than the near-null PRS-only AUROC/R2 seen for PGS001013.

Therefore, PGS004606 is the best single pick from the fixed candidate list for macular degeneration."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001270","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Phenotype/endpoint alignment is direct for PGS001270: trait_reported and trait_efo are both multiple sclerosis and phenotyping_reported is multiple sclerosis, which is the primary endpoint-fidelity field (prs_model_evaluator skill section: trait_labels). Among the direct-match candidates, PGS001270 has the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence because it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.6586; PGS R2 no covariates 0.0290) in addition to full-model metrics and incremental AUROC; this is preferred over relying on full-model AUROC alone (PGS000809, PGS002726, PGS004699) or partial correlation without AUC/R2 (PGS001831, PGS002038), per the guidance on interpreting performance fields (prs_model_evaluator skill section: performance_metrics). PGS001271 is slightly less endpoint-faithful for a generic MS risk target because it is explicitly time-to-event framed (trait_labels warning signal). Heritability sanity-check: EUR LDSC records for MS show liability-scale h2 in the ~0.09–0.16 range across ICD10/self-report MS definitions, so a PGS-only R2 around 0.03 is plausible and not obviously inconsistent with a genetic ceiling (get_heritability_records: multiple sclerosis)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001255","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity (trait_labels skill): both candidates align on trait_efo=otosclerosis and have acceptable direct disease endpoints in phenotyping_reported. However, PGS001255 uses a time-to-event (TTE) otosclerosis endpoint, which is a mild warning signal versus a generic case/control label when all else is equal; PGS002046 is labeled simply “Otosclerosis” with a straightforward phenotyping_reported field.

Performance evidence (performance_metrics skill): despite the TTE endpoint, PGS001255 provides the most directly comparable PRS evidence because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics in Europeans (PGS-only AUROC=0.6319; PGS-only R²=0.01341). Its covariates are basic (age, sex, array, PCs), reducing concern that performance is driven by heavy clinical packaging. PGS002046 lacks AUROC/R² here and only reports partial correlation (partial-r=0.0182), which is less complete/standard for choosing a single best PGS.

Heritability sanity-check (local EUR LDSC records for otosclerosis-related UKB endpoints): observed-scale h2 is low (~0.0023–0.0076 across ICD10 H80 and self-reported otosclerosis records; liability-scale values are much higher but prevalence-dependent). PGS001255’s PRS-only R² (~0.013) is not obviously inconsistent with these noisy, endpoint-dependent h2 records and supports a modest PRS signal rather than an implausibly inflated metric.

Balancing endpoint-type caution against stronger PRS-comparable metric availability, PGS001255 is the best-supported candidate in this fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000903","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait/endpoint alignment (prs_model_evaluator skill_overview + trait_labels): the target is generic Parkinson disease risk. PGS000903 has coherent direct-disease labeling across trait_reported (Parkinson’s disease), trait_efo (Parkinson disease), and phenotyping_reported (Parkinson’s disease). Several other candidates are less endpoint-faithful for this target because phenotyping_reported is progression/dementia/time-to-event decline (PGS000056 cognitive decline; PGS000211 motor decline; PGS000777 Parkinson’s disease dementia), which trait_labels flags as weaker matches than a direct diagnosis endpoint when the target is generic disease.

Performance/covariate interpretability (prs_model_evaluator performance_metrics): no candidate reports clearly labeled PGS-only AUROC/R², so full-model AUROC values are not treated as PRS-only discrimination. In that setting, PGS000903 stands out by providing more interpretable quantitative evidence of PRS contribution than most alternatives: it reports an R² (0.054) and strong stratification (OR 6.25 top vs bottom quartile), with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), whereas some higher-AUROC models rely on heavier clinical packaging (e.g., family history and multiple risk factors in PGS001774), which the skill warns can inflate full-model discrimination and reduce comparability.

Study/method strength: PGS000903 is a genome-wide C+T PRS with broad variant coverage (1,805 variants) trained on a very large PD meta-analysis (samples_training n=1,473,098), a strong structural signal versus genome-wide-significant-only scores with tens of variants when aiming to capture polygenic signal for PD risk.

Heritability sanity check (get_heritability_records, EUR): local records for Parkinson disease show non-trivial SNP-heritability on the liability scale (e.g., h2_liability ~0.086–0.174 from LDSC sources). An R² around 0.054 is plausible relative to this ceiling and not obviously inconsistent, supporting that PGS000903’s reported variance explained is within a reasonable range."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000136","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity (prs_model_evaluator: trait_labels): PGS000133–PGS000136 are coherent direct schizophrenia endpoints across trait_reported, trait_efo, and phenotyping_reported, matching the target trait cleanly. PGS002785 is not endpoint-aligned because its phenotyping_reported is cognitive function, so it is not a direct schizophrenia predictor despite the trait_reported label.

Performance interpretation (prs_model_evaluator: performance_metrics + skill_overview): none of the direct-match schizophrenia scores report PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is only supportive and should be compared cautiously; effect sizes (OR per SD) are meaningful supportive signals when available, and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/platform/batch) are relatively clean.

Within the direct-match sibling set from the same publication/method family (PRS-CS), PGS000136 is preferred because it combines (a) better supportive discrimination than the lowest siblings (full-model AUROC 0.64 vs 0.60 for PGS000133/PGS000134) and (b) a strong reported OR per SD (~1.7), indicating meaningful PRS signal. PGS000135’s higher AUROC (0.74) is based on a much smaller validation sample (n=9,569) and lacks an effect-size signal, making it less reliable as a primary pick.

Heritability sanity check (get_heritability_records: schizophrenia): EUR records show substantial SNP-heritability on the liability scale (multiple entries around h2_liability ~0.24–0.31), consistent with expecting a meaningful PRS contribution but not justifying over-weighting a single small-N AUROC outlier. This supports choosing the more stable, effect-size-supported direct schizophrenia model (PGS000136)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000471","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: Per the trait-labels guidance, phenotyping_reported is the primary endpoint-fidelity field. All three candidates have phenotyping_reported = “Carcinoma in situ of skin” and trait_reported/trait_efo also directly match “skin carcinoma in situ”, so endpoint alignment does not differentiate them.

Comparable performance evidence: Per the performance-metrics guidance, the reported AUROC/R² here are full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only), but because all three models are evaluated with the same light covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and are from the same publication family, these metrics are still useful for within-set comparison. PGS000471 has the strongest validation signals: highest AUROC (0.569), highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0255), and strongest effect sizes (OR per SD 1.401; top 1% vs rest OR 3.77), exceeding PGS000470 and PGS000469.

Heritability sanity check: Local EUR heritability records matching ICD10 D04 carcinoma in situ of skin show low observed-scale h2 (~0.0007–0.0041; liability-scale estimates higher but with low z-scores). This supports interpreting the modest R²/AUROC values as plausible and not obviously inflated by covariates or reporting artifacts.

Given identical endpoint fidelity and broadly comparable study context across candidates, PGS000471 is the best-supported choice among the fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003213","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait/endpoint alignment: The target is sleep apnea. Per the trait-labels guidance, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is the clinically dominant subtype of sleep apnea, so OSA-labeled models are still direct matches when their endpoint is coherent; however, endpoint fidelity is primarily judged by phenotyping_reported. In this list, the ExPRSweb models (PGS003204–PGS003218) have phenotyping_reported = Sleep Apnea (direct), while some OSA candidates include BMI-adjusted endpoints/covariates that change comparability.

Performance evidence and covariates: Per the performance-metrics guidance, full-model AUROC is not a reliable cross-model ranking metric when PGS-only metrics are missing, and heavier clinical covariates (e.g., BMI) can inflate AUROC. The high AUROCs (~0.77–0.79) in PGS003857/PGS003858/PGS005219/PGS005220 are reported with BMI included (and in some cases BMI-adjusted phenotyping), so they are less informative about standalone PRS quality than the ExPRSweb sleep-apnea models that use only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch/array).

Best within the clean, direct-endpoint cluster: Among the ExPRSweb sleep-apnea candidates with comparable basic covariates, PGS003213 (PRS-CS; UKB-trained) has the highest reported AUROC (0.527, CI 0.517–0.536) and the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.106, CI 1.071–1.142), making it the best-supported pick from the fixed list, though overall discrimination is weak.

Heritability sanity check: EUR heritability records for sleep apnoea show low observed-scale h2 (~0.003–0.006; liability-scale ~0.067–0.146), consistent with expecting modest PRS performance and supporting the conclusion that even the best available candidate here is sub-optimal rather than high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000014","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Grounded in prs_model_evaluator guidance (skill_overview + performance_metrics + publication_context) and trait h2 lookup: (1) Endpoint fidelity is direct: PGS000014 targets Type 2 diabetes and maps to EFO type 2 diabetes mellitus. (2) Per performance_metrics guidance, PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only / covariate-adjusted R2) are preferred over full-model AUROC/C-index that can be inflated by clinical covariates; PGS000014 reports a clear PGS-only/covariate-adjusted Nagelkerke R2=0.029, whereas many alternatives report only full-model discrimination with heavy clinical predictors (BMI, family history, glucose/lipids), making cross-model comparison less reliable. (3) Method/coverage: LDpred with ~6.9M variants and large EUR training (n=120,280) plus large validation (n=288,978) supports robustness. (4) Publication context: its Nat Genet study is disease-focused on common-disease polygenic scores rather than a pan-phenome framework score, reducing the risk of selecting a non-optimized per-trait model. (5) Heritability sanity-check: EUR h2 records for type 2 diabetes show observed h2 roughly ~0.07–0.14 (liability ~0.09–0.17 in several records), so an R2 of 0.029 is plausible and not suspiciously inflated, supporting interpretability of the reported PRS contribution."}
